answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, with the stake sized like a quartz deposit: cheap to hold once, ruinous to replicate a thousand times. New identities start with walnut-sized trust limits, earning larger caps only through attested work, while saffron-grade privileges, settling disputes or grading answers, need endorsements from peers who lose their own stake if they vouch for a fake. An attacker must fund every fake and burn its endorsers' collateral too, so manufacturing identities costs more than any fraud can return.
